subject: math
title: Add and Subtract Multi-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Multi-Digit Addition and Subtraction Worksheets: Regrouping, Subtracting Across Zeros and Word Problems
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standard_text: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 worksheets for adding and subtracting 4-, 5- and 6-digit numbers with the standard algorithm: regrouping, subtracting across zeros, missing numbers, estimating to check and word problems. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: Line up the places. Start with the ones. Regroup when you need to.
key_sub: Adding: a column of 10 or more sends 1 to the next place. Subtracting: if the top digit is smaller, take 1 from the next place, and zeros you pass become 9. Check by adding back or estimating.
body_html:
The idea: line up the places

Big numbers work just like small ones. Write them in columns so ones are under ones, tens under tens, and so on up to the hundred thousands. Then work one place at a time, starting with the ones on the right.

When a column adds up to 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup 1 to the next place on the left.

Subtract with regrouping

If the top digit is smaller than the bottom digit, regroup: take 1 from the next place on the left and make 10 more in this place. Cross out the old digit and write the new one above it.

Subtract across zeros

When the next place is 0, there is nothing to take. Keep moving left to the first digit that is not 0. Take 1 from it. Every 0 you passed becomes 9, and the column you started in gets 10 more.

Subtract across zeros

What is 10,000 − 3,467?

Regroup 1 ten thousand: 9 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 7 = 3. Tens: 9 − 6 = 3. Hundreds: 9 − 4 = 5. Thousands: 9 − 3 = 6.

Answer: 6,533

Check your answer

Add back. Addition and subtraction undo each other. Add your answer to the number you took away: 27,237 + 12,768 = 40,005, so the subtraction is right.

Estimate. Round each number to the nearest thousand and do the easy problem. 45,867 + 38,596 is about 46,000 + 39,000 = 85,000, so 84,463 makes sense. An answer like 73,353 is too far away.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the regrouped 1 (45,867 + 38,596 = 73,353)Write a small 1 above the next column and add it in
Taking the smaller digit from the bigger one (7,352 − 2,874 = 5,522)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Regroup when the top is smaller
Regrouping but not crossing out (7,352 − 2,874 = 5,588)When you take 1 from a place, that digit gets 1 smaller
Changing zeros to 10 instead of 9 (10,000 − 3,467 = 7,643)Each 0 you pass gives 1 to the right, so it becomes 9
Lining up the numbers on the left (48,307 + 6,895)Line up the ones on the right. Commas line up too

faq.q: What is the standard algorithm for addition and subtraction?
faq.a: It is the column method: line up the numbers by place value, start with the ones, and regroup when a column needs it. Grade 4 students use it with numbers up to 1,000,000.

faq.q: How do you subtract across zeros, like 40,005 − 12,768?
faq.a: Go left to the first digit that is not 0 and take 1 from it. Every 0 you pass becomes 9 and the ones get 10 more, so 40,005 becomes 3 ten thousands, 9 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 15 ones. Then subtract each place to get 27,237.

faq.q: How can my child check a multi-digit subtraction answer?
faq.a: Add the answer to the number that was subtracted. If you get the starting number, the answer is right: 27,237 + 12,768 = 40,005. A quick estimate, like 40,000 − 13,000 = 27,000, also catches big mistakes.
It is the Common Core standard for Grade 4: fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm. In Grade 4 the numbers go up to 1,000,000.

sets.title: Word problems, missing numbers and estimates

items.q: What number goes in the box? 245,318 + ☐ = 600,000
items.e: Use subtraction: 600,000 − 245,318. Line up the places and start with the ones. Ones: 0 − 8 needs a regroup, but there are 0 tens, 0 hundreds, 0 thousands and 0 ten thousands. Regroup across the zeros: 6 hundred thousands become 5, each 0 becomes 9, and the ones become 10. 10 − 8 = 2. The other places subtract without regrouping. Answer: 354,682. Check: 354,682 + 245,318 = 600,000.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 82,040 − ☐ = 35,678
A stadium has 68,450 seats. At a football game, 52,786 seats were filled. How many seats were empty?
items.e: Take the filled seats away from all the seats: subtract. Line up the places and start with the ones. Ones: 0 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 10 − 6 = 4. Tens: 4 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 hundred becomes 10 tens: 14 − 8 = 6. Hundreds: 3 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 thousand becomes 10 hundreds: 13 − 7 = 6. The other places subtract without regrouping. Answer: 15,664. Check: 15,664 + 52,786 = 68,450.

items.q: An orchard had 25,640 apples in storage. It sold 8,975 apples and then picked 6,380 more. How many apples are in storage now?
items.e: Step 1, after selling: 25,640 − 8,975 = 16,665. Step 2, after picking: 16,665 + 6,380 = 23,045. Check with estimates: 26,000 − 9,000 + 6,000 = 23,000.

items.q: Mount Everest is 29,032 feet tall. Mount Whitney is 14,505 feet tall. How much taller is Mount Everest?
items.e: How much taller means find the difference: subtract. Line up the places and start with the ones. Ones: 2 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 12 − 5 = 7. Hundreds: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 thousand becomes 10 hundreds: 10 − 5 = 5. The other places subtract without regrouping. Answer: 14,527. Check: 14,527 + 14,505 = 29,032.

items.q: Lily added 46,215 + 27,890 and got 64,105. Round each number to the nearest thousand to check. What does the estimate show?
items.e: Estimate: 46,000 + 28,000 = 74,000, but Lily's answer is about 64,000, so it is about 10,000 too small. She forgot the regrouped 1 in the ten thousands. The correct sum is 74,105.

items.q: A pilot named Emma flew 23,684 miles in May and 19,857 miles in June. How many miles did she fly in the two months?
items.e: Put the two distances together: add. Line up the places and start with the ones. Ones: 4 + 7 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 8 + 5 + 1 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 6 + 8 + 1 = 15, write 5 and regroup 1 thousand. Thousands: 3 + 9 + 1 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 ten thousand. The other places add without regrouping. Answer: 43,541. Check: 43,541 − 19,857 = 23,684.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ − 15,394 = 48,726
items.e: The box is the starting number, so add: 48,726 + 15,394 = 64,120. Check: 64,120 − 15,394 = 48,726.

items.q: A factory made 14,268 toy cars on Monday. On Tuesday, it made 2,795 more toy cars than on Monday. How many toy cars did it make on both days?
Round each number to the nearest thousand. Which is the best estimate for 72,309 − 28,746?
items.e: 72,309 rounds to 72,000 and 28,746 rounds to 29,000. 72,000 − 29,000 = 43,000. The exact answer, 43,563, is close to 43,000.

items.q: A school wants to raise $20,000 for a new playground. So far it has raised $12,450. How much more money does it need?
items.e: Find what is missing from the goal: subtract. Line up the places and start with the ones. Tens: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but there are 0 hundreds and 0 thousands. Regroup across the zeros: 2 ten thousands become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the tens become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. The other places subtract without regrouping. Answer: 7,550. Check: 7,550 + 12,450 = 20,000.

items.q: An airport had 186,394 passengers in June and 207,758 passengers in July. How many passengers did it have in the two months?
items.e: Put the two months together: add. Line up the places and start with the ones. Ones: 4 + 8 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 9 + 5 + 1 = 15, write 5 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 3 + 7 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 thousand. Thousands: 6 + 7 + 1 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 ten thousand. The other places add without regrouping. Answer: 394,152. Check: 394,152 − 207,758 = 186,394.
